title: Gravitational Orbit & Collision Lab
description: A WaterBottle orbits a massive ShaderBall2 acting as a gravitational attractor on a dark space-themed stage. The user adjusts orbital parameters—gravity strength, initial velocity, damping, and mass ratio—then launches the bottle and observes realistic orbital mechanics including elastic collisions, energy transfer, and trajectory trails.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a gravitational orbit and collision physics sandbox.

SCENE SETUP: Dark background (0x0a0a1a) with subtle star-field particles (200 small white points). Place ShaderBall2.glb at the world origin scaled to roughly 1.5 units—it represents a massive planetary body with a subtle emissive glow ring around it (use a torus with emissive material). Place WaterBottle.glb at position (5, 0, 0) scaled appropriately as the orbiting projectile. Use PerspectiveCamera at (0, 8, 12) looking at origin. Add AmbientLight (intensity 0.3) and one DirectionalLight (intensity 1.2) from upper-right. Use OrbitControls for camera.

PHYSICS ENGINE (custom, no library): Implement Newtonian gravity F=G*m1*m2/r^2 between the bottle and the shader ball. Track velocity and position each frame using Verlet integration. Detect sphere-based collision between the two objects; on collision apply elastic bounce with energy loss coefficient. Draw a fading trajectory trail behind the bottle using a BufferGeometry line that stores the last 300 positions with vertex colors fading from cyan to transparent.

INTERACTION STEPS (6 required validated inputs): (1) A slider 'Gravity Constant G' range 0.1–5.0 default 1.0. (2) A slider 'Initial Tangential Velocity' range 0.5–4.0 default 2.0. (3) A slider 'Bottle Mass' range 0.1–3.0 default 1.0. (4) A slider 'ShaderBall Mass' range 5–50 default 20. (5) A slider 'Damping Factor' range 0.9–1.0 step 0.005 default 0.998. (6) A 'Launch' button that resets the bottle to start position and begins simulation with current parameters. Display a real-time HUD showing current orbital speed, distance from center, and kinetic energy. Validate all parameters are within range before launch. Style the control panel as a translucent dark overlay on the left side with white text. Pause physics until Launch is clicked. Add a 'Reset' button to stop simulation and return bottle to initial position.
